title: Research on Mobile Robot Path Planning Based on Improved Crested Porcupine Optimizer
content: The application of the Crested Porcupine Optimizer (CPO) to global path planning for mobile robots is hindered by several inherent deficiencies, such as non-uniform initialization, inadequate population diversity, susceptibility to local optima stagnation, an imbalance between global exploration and local exploitation, and limited local exploitation capability. To overcome these limitations, this study introduces a multi-mechanism collaborative improved Crested Porcupine Optimizer (ICPO). The proposed ICPO incorporates four strategic improvements: (1) initialization based on high-quality point sets to ensure uniform population distribution; (2) a failed-memory odor repulsion mechanism to avoid invalid repeated searches and sustain population diversity; (3) a quality-crowding multi-scale attack strategy to precisely regulate the exploration-exploitation balance; and (4) dynamic neighborhood-based local visual perception to effectively strengthen the algorithm’s ability to escape from local optima. Comparative experiments against the Conventional CPO, the Sparrow Search Algorithm (SSA), and the Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO) validate the superiority of ICPO across varying environmental complexities. Results indicate that in 2D grid maze environments, ICPO reduces planning runtime by 75.81% and shortens path lengths by 15.95% relative to the baseline CPO, thereby enhancing both computational efficiency and path optimality. In 3D complex terrain scenarios, ICPO achieves reductions of 39.47% in computation time and 15.31% in path length compared to conventional CPO, demonstrating robust adaptability. Moreover, ICPO outperforms SSA and GWO in generating optimal paths with lower computational overhead, confirming its comprehensive advantages in robotic path planning.
